purpose: Project-aware production orchestration platform across games, websites, apps, media, providers, QA and release governance.
rules: Never commit or echo secret values.
Prefer Game Shop orchestration, but preserve direct provider MCP/API/SDK access.
For real product work, select the project and load gameshop_mission_context before planning or execution.
The first-party web console is an MCP client, not a second orchestration implementation; server-side scopes and policy gates remain authoritative.
Client-mediated handoffs are task packets for the connected specialist/plugin/local workspace; never falsely claim the Vercel server executed them.
Server-direct execution is limited to verified adapters and runtime credentials/policy gates.
Execute scope alone must never mutate project source; source repair requires Write, and the combined repair+rereun tool requires Write + QA.
Preserve independent Read, Plan, QA, Execute, Write and Deploy permissions.
Route game work through the smallest specialist set that satisfies the task; never migrate engines merely because another engine is available.
Route website work through the smallest stack that satisfies the task; do not add backend, commerce or 3D infrastructure merely because it is available.
Route app work through the smallest valid web/native stack; browser QA alone is not sufficient evidence for native behavior.
Preserve approved media masters and distinguish generated derivatives from source assets.
For existing products, inspect and repair incrementally before considering framework or architecture migration.
Paid generation must remain blocked unless GAME_SHOP_ALLOW_PAID_GENERATION=true.
Do not automatically retry a possibly-submitted paid generation on another provider.
gameshop_release_mission must use the strict persisted-evidence release governor and Deploy scope.
Use ecosystem.json and mcp.json as machine-readable snapshots; regenerate them after catalog/routing changes.
Keep generated artifacts in the universal artifact lifecycle and route ready artifacts through persistence/placement/verification/QA where applicable.

preferredLLMWorkflow.browserConsole: /console via OAuth PKCE + live MCP tool discovery
preferredLLMWorkflow.missionControl: gameshop_mission_projects → gameshop_mission_context → gameshop_plan_mission → gameshop_execute_mission_handoff → execution adapter/client bridge → automatic QA → repair+rereun → approve → release
preferredLLMWorkflow.missionExecution: gameshop_mission_execution_adapters → gameshop_execute_mission_adapter for server-direct/client-bridge execution; never use generic Execute for source writes
preferredLLMWorkflow.automaticQa: gameshop_qa_capture_mission; after an external repair use gameshop_qa_repair_and_rerun; for an approved GitHub patch use gameshop_apply_patch_mission_and_rerun with Write + QA
preferredLLMWorkflow.providerExecute: gameshop_run_provider_task with execute=true only when explicitly intended
